motivatingPathology: This baseline is deliberately unminimized: a real one-page document carrying an embedded chart part, a footer part, and a styles part alongside the body. Hand-built fixtures prove single pathologies; this one proves the round trip holds when chart markup, footer references, and latent styles ride along unexamined. If a future engine change breaks real files while minimized fixtures stay green, this is the fixture that catches it.
knownLimitations: As a baseline it characterizes no single pathology, so a failure here diagnoses poorly without the minimized fixtures beside it. The chart data is not mutated and chart rendering is never compared; only byte preservation of the chart part is asserted. One chart of one type is present, so chart variety is not covered. Mutation targets stay unformatted paragraphs by rule; replace now carries the first run's properties onto rewritten text, so the rule is conservative rather than required.
scopeExclusions: This fixture does not isolate any pathology: merges, revisions, drawings, numbering, and notes appear only if the source file happens to contain them. Minimized coverage lives in the hand-built fixtures, not here. Rendered equivalence of the chart and footer belongs to a layout study, not to this structural gate.
ecma376Difficulty: Real files bundle independent parts that reference each other through relationships: the document points at the chart and footer parts, each with content-type declarations that must survive. A writer that rewrites only the parts it models and drops the rest will validate the body while silently losing the chart. The difficulty is negative: success means touching nothing except the two mutated sentences.
licenseProvenance: Copied byte-identical from the in-repo test gallery; same repository license as the gallery source; no new provenance claims.

disposition.reason: The gallery file is Word-legal throughout, so the engine preserves every part: only the two mutated sentences change, all other parts are byte-identical, and the package validates clean.
